text:
Winnipeg led after the first period's chances and still found itself chasing the game by the end. WPG held the edge in expected goals in the opening 20 minutes (1.02 to 0.69), but nobody scored. Then Carolina took over the second, out-chancing the Jets 1.43 to 0.51, and it never gave that control back.

The scoring came in a burst. Mark Scheifele opened it with a backhand at 4:23 of the second, and Mark Jankowski answered on the power play at 8:19. Alex Iafallo tipped one in to put WPG back in front, and Jesperi Kotkaniemi tipped one of his own at 16:50 to make it 2-2. Nikolaj Ehlers broke the tie with a power-play slap shot at 6:43 of the third, assisted by Shayne Gostisbehere, who finished with two assists and was on the ice for 1.29 expected goals for against 0.36 against.

The final score hid how lopsided the game was. CAR finished with 74 shot attempts to 50 and 3.38 expected goals to 2.38, which gives the Hurricanes a 67 percent share of simulated replays. Both goalies, Pyotr Kochetkov and Clay Stevenson, finished 0.38 goals better than expected. The difference was special teams: CAR went 2 for 2 on the power play, WPG 0 for 1, and the two power-play goals made up the gap between the sides.
